components.assumption: On a publish day and the 1 day(s) after, downloads above the median of the 7 quiet days before are mirrors, registries, scanners and Dependabot/Renovate fetching the new version, not new users. 4 release(s) in the window. When release days cover more than 40% of the window there is no quiet baseline and nothing is removed here.

components.label: Flat automation (same every day of the week)
components.assumption: People work weekdays. Human-driven traffic on a weekend day is 0.48x a weekday (measured, see README). Whatever does not follow that rhythm is cron jobs, scheduled CI and bots: 3975 a day here. Push-triggered CI follows the human week and is NOT removed by this step.

components.label: Human-rhythm fresh resolves (the real part, upper bound)
components.assumption: What is left: newest-in-line downloads on quiet days that follow the working week. It still includes push-triggered CI that resolves without a lockfile, so it is an upper bound on people. It also keeps 62190 downloads (6.7%) from rarely used old lines that were not fetched one by one, which makes it generous, not harsh.
